answer_1.quote: We conduct extensive experiments on commonsense story and fiction generation tasks. ... We evaluate HINT on ROCStories (ROC for short) and Writing-Prompts (WP for short).
answer_1.outputs: Generated multi‑sentence stories (long texts) conditioned on a prompt or first sentence

answer_2.quote: We adopt the following automatic metrics to evaluate the performance on the test sets: (1) Perplexity (PPL)... (2) BLEU (B-n)... (3) Lexical Repetition (LR-n)... (4) Semantic Repetition (SR-n)... (5) Distinct-4 (D-4)... (6) Context Relatedness... (7) Sentence Orders...

answer_4.quote: We adopt majority voting to make final decisions among the three annotators. We resort to Amazon Mechanical Turk (AMT) for annotation... We follow to define fluency as a measure of intra‑sentence linguistic quality and grammatical correctness, and coherence as inter‑sentence relatedness, causal and temporal dependencies.
answer_4.guideline: Workers were shown an input and two generated texts (one by HINT and one by a baseline) and asked to select the better text in terms of fluency and coherence; they also annotated specific error types (repetition, unrelatedness, wrong temporal orders, others).
